# Coming from QuickBASIC 4.5

<!-- Written by tools/reference/reference.py render; do not edit. -->

Where QB64Rust does something other than QuickBASIC 4.5. Most rows are QB64pe's behavior, which
QB64Rust keeps; the QuickBASIC column says whether it was measured, documented or believed.
37 rows, from `docs/DIVERGENCES-QB45.md`, which also says why each was decided and what pins it.

| Id | Case | QuickBASIC 4.5 | QB64Rust |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q-001 | `ON n GOTO` / `ON n GOSUB` with `n` above 255 | Error 5, "Illegal function call" (`n` must be 0 to 255) | Continues with the next statement, as for `n` = 0 or `n` beyond the number of labels; a negative `n` raises error 5 in both |
| Q-002 | `SELECT CASE` in a recursive procedure: the copy of the test expression | Kept in the procedure's stack frame, so each call has its own and a recursive call between the test and a later `CASE` does not change it | One static copy per `SELECT` statement (QB64pe since its first version, `qb64pe.bas` "static … sc_"), so a recursive call overwrites it and the outer `SELECT` tests the inner call's value at its later `CASE`s (`verification\v04_accidental`) |
| Q-003 | Division by zero with an `ON ERROR` handler: integer `\` and `MOD` by 0, `ERROR 11`, a float `/` by 0 | Integer `\`, `MOD` and `ERROR 11`: error 11, "Division by zero", trapped by the handler. A float `/` by 0 gives infinity (`1.#INF`), with no error | Integer `\`, `MOD` and `ERROR 11`: error 11, trapped, as QB 4.5 (`DIVERGENCES-QB64PE.md` D-052, OpenSpec change `libqb-fixes`; `verification\v63_e1`, `e2`). A float `/` by 0 gives infinity with no error, as QB 4.5 does too |
| Q-004 | INTEGER arithmetic beyond the INTEGER range inside an expression (`i% = 32767: PRINT i% + 1`) | Error 6, "Overflow", also when the result is stored into a LONG (`l& = i% + 1`). A LONG beyond its range raises error 6 too | Computed in 32 bits: prints 32768; only the store into an INTEGER wraps (`i% = i% + 1` gives -32768). LONG wraps too (`DIVERGENCES-QB64PE.md` D-001) |
| Q-005 | The initial bytes of a fixed-length string (`DIM f AS STRING * 4`, also in a `TYPE`) | NUL bytes (0), as QB64pe, for a variable, a member, an element and a local `DIM` on each call; assignment pads with spaces. **Not a divergence**: the row was entered when QB 4.5 was believed to give spaces | NUL bytes (0); assignment still pads with spaces (`verification\v03_storage`) |
| Q-006 | `PRINT` with a comma when the program writes to the console (`$CONSOLE`), e.g. a QB 4.5 screen program built as `$CONSOLE:ONLY` | 14-column zones on the screen (QB 4.5 has no console) | Windows console: 10-column zones; Linux and macOS console: one space (read, not run); window and files: 14-column zones (`study\00` §6, `DIVERGENCES-QB64PE.md` D-011) |
| Q-007 | `STRING$(n, "")` | Error 5, "Illegal function call", also when `n` is 0 | Reads the first byte of the empty string (`verification\v20_c_string_edges`; `n` = 0 not measured there) |
| Q-008 | `CONST c = 2 ^ 3 ^ 2` (a chain of `^` in a `CONST`) | A compile error, "Syntax error", for any `^` in a `CONST`, also a single `CONST b = 2 ^ 3`. At run time the chain is left-associative: 64 | Right-associative in a `CONST` only: 512 (64 at run time), with a compiler warning (`verification\v17_e_const`) |
| Q-009 | An array used without `DIM` inside a SUB or FUNCTION (`x(2) = 5` with no array `x` declared there) | A compiler warning, "Array not dimensioned", then a working array 0 to 10 that keeps its values between calls, in a SUB, a FUNCTION and a `SUB … STATIC` alike. An index of 11 is error 9. In a plain SUB the first read gave a stray value (1.234183E-38) instead of 0 | Every use raises error 9, on every call: QB64pe makes a local dynamic array and writes nothing that allocates it; a `DIM` or `REDIM` of the name later in the procedure does. Only in a `SUB … STATIC` (not below `$DYNAMIC`) is it a working array, 0 to 10, kept between calls (`verification\v24_f_implicit_sub`, `v24_x120`, `x176`) |
| Q-010 | A `SUB … STATIC` or `FUNCTION … STATIC` that holds a `STATIC` statement: the variables and arrays first named below that statement | Documented: `STATIC` after the header makes every variable of the procedure keep its value between calls | Kept only when first named above the procedure's first `STATIC` statement; below it new variables are made on each call and a `DIM` is a local dynamic array (QB64pe's flag for the procedure is reset at the end of a `STATIC` statement). A procedure without a `STATIC` statement keeps everything |
| Q-011 | A `PLAY` string with a tempo or an octave outside QuickBASIC's range (`PLAY "T31 C"`, `"T256 C"`, `"O7 C"`) | Error 5, "Illegal function call": the tempo is 32 to 255 quarter notes a minute, the octave 0 to 6 | Played with no error (libqb takes any tempo and octave it can compute with); a length of 0 or above 64, a note above 84 and an unknown command are error 5 in both |
| Q-012 | `ON PLAY(n) GOSUB`, `PLAY ON`, `PLAY OFF`, `PLAY STOP` (the event of the background music buffer) | An event: the handler runs when fewer than `n` notes are left to play | No such event. `ON PLAY(n) GOSUB label` is `ON <number> GOSUB` with the function `PLAY`; `PLAY ON`, `PLAY OFF` and `PLAY STOP` are compile errors |
| Q-013 | `LSET` with two variables of a user type (`LSET r = r2`) | Copies the bytes of one record variable into the other, also between two types | A compile error: the target of `LSET` and `RSET` is a string variable, element or member (`r = r2` copies a value of one type) |
| Q-014 | An assignment with `=` (or `INPUT`) to a string named by `FIELD` | The string is no field any more: it moves out of the record buffer | The string gets the value and its length and stays a field: the next `LSET` to any field of the file, or `GET` with no variable, gives it its width and the buffer's bytes again. A second `FIELD` on a file keeps the strings of the first as fields, as there |
| Q-015 | The number in `STATIC a(n)` (and the `STATIC` of an array in a SUB beside a shared array of that name and type) | The number of dimensions: `STATIC a(5) AS LONG` is an array of five dimensions, so `a(1)` is "Wrong number of dimensions"; the array is given bounds by a later `DIM`. Such a `STATIC` declares an array of the SUB's own, also beside a shared array of the same name and type | The upper bound: `STATIC a(5)` is `a(0 TO 5)`. Beside a shared array of the same name and type QB64pe allocates the shared one again (`verification\v24_x272`, `v55_d1`); this compiler makes it the SUB's own, always for a static shared array (`DIVERGENCES-QB64PE.md` D-041) and with the fix `static-local-dynamic` for a dynamic one |
| Q-016 | The number 0 as the upper bound of an array under `OPTION BASE 1` (`DIM x(0)`, `REDIM x(0)`, `REDIM x(n)` with `n` = 0) | `DIM x(0)` and `REDIM x(0)`: "Lower bound exceeds upper bound" at compile time (the bounds are 1 TO 0); `REDIM x(n)` with `n` = 0: error 9 at run time, and the array is then not allocated | The number 0 written in plain digits keeps its dimension 0 TO 0: `DIM x(0)` and `REDIM x(0)` compile and have one element (`verification\v64_b4`, `b5`). `REDIM x(n)` with `n` = 0, or `x(0 + 0)`: error 5, "Illegal function call", after which `LBOUND` is 1 and `UBOUND` 0 (`v64_b5`). A member array has no such rule: `z(0)` in a `TYPE` and `REDIM t.v(0)` under base 1 are "Invalid array bounds", as in QB 4.5 (`v64_b1`–`b3`) |
| Q-017 | The compiler's message for an array used without `DIM` (`z(2) = 5` with no array `z` declared), in the main module or in a SUB or FUNCTION | A warning, "Array not dimensioned", at the first use of each such array; the program still builds. What the array then does: Q-009 | No message, in the main module and in procedures. QB64pe's build of `verification\v24_f_implicit_sub` records only `exit=0`, and `qb64rust --dump typed` of `q45_implicit_sub` lists the arrays and reports nothing |
| Q-018 | A SUB that ends at `END SUB` (measured; `EXIT SUB` is believed the same) with its own `GOSUB` still pending, called while the main module's `GOSUB` is pending | The SUB's entry is dropped when the SUB ends. The main module's next `RETURN` goes back to its own `GOSUB` | One `GOSUB` stack for the whole program: the SUB's entry stays on it. The main module's next `RETURN` takes that entry, finds no match and raises error 3, "RETURN without GOSUB". The World War 2 game's editor stopped this way: its `menu` SUB leaves `GOSUB selex` by `GOTO` when an item is picked by its letter |
| Q-019 | Where the lines of a `DRAW` string end at scale 6 (`S6`; other scales than 4 are believed alike, not measured). Measured with the small train of Civil War Strategy: `PSET (550, 20)`, then `DRAW "C15S6R9D4R6U3R3D3R7U5H3U2R9D3G2D6F1D3F5L10D1G1L4H2L7G2L3H2L3U8L2U5R1BF4"` | The graphics cursor ends at 555, 26. The outline is closed: `PAINT` inside it stays inside | The cursor ends at 556, 28, in QB64pe and QB64Rust alike. The outline's last line is two rows below its first, so the outline is open by one pixel row and `PAINT` inside it covers the screen. The game's port changes one length of the string (`U8` to `U9`) |
| Q-020 | The pixels of `CIRCLE` with an aspect and with start and end angles. Measured with the cannon's wheel of Civil War Strategy, centered at 595, 380: `CIRCLE (x, y), 25, 1, , , 1.4`, the arc `CIRCLE (x + 5, y), 29, 1, 4, 1.5, 1.4` and `CIRCLE (x, y), 29, 1, , , 1.4`, then `PAINT (618, 373), 5, 1` | The point 618, 373 is inside the crescent between the outer ellipse and the arc. The paint stays there | The point is outside the arc, in QB64pe and QB64Rust alike, and the paint covers the screen. The game's port gives the arc the radius 27 |
| Q-021 | The type of a SINGLE constant times a LONG: `.01 * s&` with `s& = 69` | DOUBLE: `WRITE #` gives `.6899999845772982` (PDS 7.1: `.689999984577298`, 15 digits), the SINGLE `.01` widened and multiplied exactly. Assigned to a DOUBLE it is the same number | SINGLE: `WRITE #` gives `.69`. Assigned to a DOUBLE it is `.6900000000000001`. Assigned to a SINGLE or an INTEGER, all four compilers agree. **Written by `WRITE #` and read back by `INPUT #` into an INTEGER, it gives one more for `s& = 150, 350, 550` and every 200 after.** QB64 writes `1.5`, `3.5`, `5.5`, and `INPUT #` rounds a half to the even integer in all four compilers (`"1.5"` gives 2, `"2.5"` gives 2). The old compilers write `1.49999996647239`, which reads as 1. That is 15 values of 0 to 3,000. **Writing the constant as a SINGLE does not help:** `.01! * CDBL(s&)` and `CSNG(.01) * CDBL(s&)` still multiply by the DOUBLE 0.01 (`1.5` for 150), where the old compilers widen the SINGLE. Only a SINGLE variable, `k! = .01: k! * CDBL(s&)`, gives the old compilers' product, and the same text as QB 4.5 (`1.499999966472387`) |
| Q-022 | A SINGLE constant times an INTEGER, assigned to an INTEGER: `x = .7 * x` with `x = 165` (115.4999980…) and `x = 385` (269.4999954…), as in Wars of Napoleon's battles | The product is rounded to the INTEGER from its exact value: 115 and 269 | The product is first rounded to a SINGLE, which is 115.5 and 269.5, then to the INTEGER by banker's rounding: 116 and 270. In the same program, 118 other products and sums of this kind (`.8 * a + .2 * b`) and 200 results of a sum of twelve `RND`s times `SQR` came out the same in all four compilers. **A comparison rounds the same way.** `c >= .2 * a` with `c = 15`, `a = 75` is false in the old compilers (15.0000002) and true in QB64 (15). It is the same for every multiple of 5 from 5 to 1000: false for all 200 in QB 4.5 and PDS 7.1, true for all 200 in QB64pe and QB64Rust. With the product stored in a SINGLE variable first, all four give true. Wars of Napoleon's supply test `IF cash(s) >= .2 * armysize(i)` met it in a recorded session (its `docs\devnotes.md`, "Session 5's missing wait") |
| Q-023 | The pixels of text in `SCREEN 9` and `SCREEN 10` (the 8 × 14 font) | The video BIOS's own 8 × 14 font. In DOSBox-X, `U` is 9 rows tall and starts on row 2 of its cell | No 8 × 14 font of its own: libqb draws rows 1 to 14 of each 8 × 16 glyph (`study\03` "The 8x14 font"). `U` is 10 rows tall and starts on row 1, so a cell of text differs from DOSBox-X's by 3 to 7 pixels. The 8 × 16 font of `SCREEN 12` and `SCREEN 0` is the same pixel for pixel: in 313 DOSBox-X screenshots (640 × 480 and 720 × 400), 27,614 cells match a QB64 glyph exactly, and the few near misses are text over a map line |
| Q-024 | Where the style of `LINE (x1, y1)-(x2, y2), c, , style` starts: `LINE (42, 10)-(10, 10), 15, , &H1111` and the same line given from the other end | The style starts at the left end of the line at every slope (flat, 45 degrees, steeper), whichever end is written first, so a line drawn from each end gets the same pixels both times. A vertical line is the exception: its style starts at the first point written, as in QB64, so `LINE (10, 10)-(10, 42)` and `LINE (10, 42)-(10, 10)` light other pixels (rows 8 and 9 of the record; corrected 2026-11-09, when Wars of Napoleon's vertical roads showed two sets of dots in DOSBox-X). Each `LINE` starts the style again, also `LINE -(x, y)` | The style starts at the first point written. A line drawn from each end gets two sets of dots, so a road of Wars of Napoleon drawn with `&H1111` from each city has twice the dots it had in DOS: `.9.F.9.F` where QB 4.5 has `...9...9`. Each `LINE` starts the style again, as in QB 4.5 |
| Q-025 | Which pixels a solid sloping `LINE` lights. Measured for every end point within 12 pixels of (50, 50), 625 lines, each drawn from both ends | The same pixels from either end. A line steps to the next row (or column) earlier than halfway: `LINE (50, 50)-(62, 51)` lights 3 pixels on row 50 and 10 on row 51. All 625 lines fit one rule: Bresenham's steps from the left end (the bottom end of a vertical line), along the longer side n, with a first error of `3 * n \ 4` | Other pixels for 492 of the 625 lines: `LINE (50, 50)-(62, 51)` lights 7 and 6. For 96 lines the pixels also depend on which end is written first. Flat, vertical and 45-degree lines are the same in all four compilers. With Q-024 fixed in the program, Wars of Napoleon's roads still had some dots one pixel to the side of DOSBox-X's. Its port now draws the roads pixel by pixel with that rule (`styledline` in its `QB64.BM`), and they then match DOSBox-X's screenshots |
| Q-026 | Whether the right side of `AND` or `OR` in a condition is evaluated when the left side already decides it: `IF y > x AND RND > .5` with `y > x` false | **QB 4.5: evaluated, as QB64.** BASIC PDS 7.1 differs: when both sides are relations, it skips the right side of `AND` when the left is false, and of `OR` when the left is true. It does so in a single-line or block `IF`, in `ELSEIF`, and in the conditions of `DO WHILE`, `DO UNTIL`, `LOOP WHILE` and `WHILE`. A side may itself be such a condition: in `IF y > x AND (RND > .5 OR x <> 1)` the whole parenthesis is skipped, and in `IF a OR b AND RND > .5` (`AND` binds closer) `RND` is called only when `a` is false and `b` true. It evaluates both sides when a side is not a relation (`IF y AND RND > .5`), for `XOR`, and for a value (`z = y > x AND RND > .5`, `PRINT`). A user FUNCTION on the right side is always called. So in a program built with PDS 7.1, an `RND` or `INKEY$` on the skipped side is not called | Both sides are evaluated in every case, as QB 4.5. A program ported from PDS 7.1 then draws an `RND` that PDS did not, and every later `RND` differs. In Wars of Napoleon, `IF y > x AND RND > .5` (its `WON1.BM` line 874) made the computer's armies move elsewhere from the first turn. And a `TICK` written as `DO WHILE TIMER - start! < sec! AND INKEY$ = ""` reads and loses a key typed ahead when its time is already up, where PDS left the key in the buffer. Written as a nested `IF` (`IF y > x THEN IF RND > .5 THEN`), a line does the same in all four compilers |
| Q-027 | `INPUT #` of a quoted field followed by more text before the comma: the line `"say "hi" now",7`, which `WRITE #` makes of the string `say "hi" now` and 7 | `WRITE #` writes the inner quotes as they are, as QB64. `INPUT #` ends the field at the second quote and starts a new field at once: three fields, `say `, `hi" now"` and `7` | The same bytes from `WRITE #`. `INPUT #` ends the field at the second quote and skips the rest up to the comma: two fields, `say ` and `7`. So a program that reads such a line into three variables gets the 7 one variable early |
| Q-028 | A number stored through a member of an element whose index calls a FUNCTION that changes the number: `a(setn(1)).k = n`, where `setn` sets `n` from 1 to 2 | The index first, then the value: 2 is stored. A string member, and a plain array of either kind, take the index first, as QB 4.5 |
| Q-029 | `LEN` of an element of a numeric or `STRING * n` array whose index calls a FUNCTION: `LEN(a(f(1)))` | The index is evaluated, so `f` is called once, but not checked: `LEN(a(9))` on `DIM a(3)` is 2 with no error, as QB64. `LEN` of a variable-length string element checks it (error 9) | The index is not evaluated: `f` is not called. The rest as QB 4.5. After the error 9 of `k = LEN(v$(9))`, `RESUME NEXT` finds `k` set to 0, where QB 4.5 left the statement undone (the bad index reading element 0, a behavior kept on 2026-10-08) |
| Q-030 | An array used without `DIM` in the main module below `'$DYNAMIC`: stored in a loop (`x(i) = i * 10` for i = 1 to 3), first named on a line a `GOTO` skips, first named in a `LOOP UNTIL` | The array is made once and works in all three: `10 20 30`, then `7`, then the loop ends at n = 3. A warning, "Array not dimensioned", at each first use (Q-017) | The statement that names it first makes it, as part of that statement. Run again, it raises error 10 and skips its store: `10 0 0` with two errors 10. Skipped by the `GOTO`, the array is never made: every later use raises 9. In `LOOP UNTIL`, error 10 on the second round ends the loop at n = 2 |
| Q-031 | The target of a `READ` that raises an error: a quoted item read into a number (`DATA "5"` into `n&`), which is error 2 in all four compilers | The target keeps its value (-1 in the measure). | Q-032 | `DIM a()` and `REDIM a()` with empty parentheses, and `REDIM a AS LONG` with none | Compile errors: "Syntax error" at the `)` of `DIM a()` and `REDIM a()`, "Left parenthesis missing" for `REDIM a AS LONG` | Accepted: each declares the scalar `a` and no array, so `a(1)` after it is another array, used without `DIM` (`verification\v24_b_dim_empty*`, `v24_x43`, `x44`, `x86`) |
| Q-033 | A unary plus before a variable (`x = +b`, `2 * +b`, `(+b)`), and doubled signs in a `CONST` (`CONST c = 2 * - -3`) | All accepted, with ordinary arithmetic: `+b` is `b`, `2 * +b` 10 with b = 5, `CONST c = 2 * - -3` is 6. | Q-034 | A second declaration without `AS` of an array typed by `AS`: `DIM c(2) AS DOUBLE` then `DIM c(3)`; `REDIM d(2) AS DOUBLE` then `REDIM d(3)` | Compile errors: "Array already dimensioned" for the `DIM`, "AS clause required" for the `REDIM` | Accepted. | Q-035 | Whether `WIDTH , 60` in `SCREEN 12` keeps a color set by `PALETTE`: `PALETTE 2, 256 * 34`, then `WIDTH , 60`, then the VGA's color registers read back (`OUT &H3C7`, `INP(&H3C9)`) | **QB 4.5 resets the palette**: entry 2 is 0, 42, 0 again after `WIDTH , 60` and after `WIDTH , 30`. **PDS 7.1 keeps it**: entry 2 stays 0, 34, 0. | Q-036 | Which pixels a small `CIRCLE` lights with the screen's own aspect: `CIRCLE (50, 50), r, 15` for each radius from 1 to 10, in `SCREEN 12` and in `SCREEN 9`, then `PAINT` inside it | QB 4.5 and PDS 7.1 light the same pixels.
